_meta: A chunk longer than the embedding model's maximum sequence length, used to show that the model silently TRUNCATES input beyond its token limit -- so content in the tail of an over-long chunk is never embedded and cannot be retrieved -- and that chunks must be sized in tokens to fit the model. Every embedding model has a maximum input length (a token count: 512 for many sentence-transformer models, larger for newer ones). Feed it more tokens than that and it does not error; it truncates, embedding only the first max_len tokens and discarding the rest. So if a chunk is longer than the limit, the embedding represents only its beginning, and any fact living past the cutoff contributes nothing to the vector -- a query that should match that fact finds no signal for it and the chunk is not retrieved, even though the text is right there in the stored chunk. The failure is silent: the embedding is produced, the pipeline runs, and the tail is simply invisible to search. The fix is to chunk so each piece fits under the model's max length, measured in the model's TOKENS (not characters or words, which under-count), or to use a long-context embedding model. chunk is the chunk's token sequence; max_len is the model's maximum token length; query_term is a term the searcher is looking for. chunk, max_len, and query_term are the fixture; the truncated embedding's terms, whether the query term survives truncation in the long chunk, and whether splitting into max_len-sized chunks recovers it are computed.
